title: The farewell tawaf
hookLine: a last circling before leaving Mecca

lines: …UNTIL THE LAST THING IS THE HOUSE.
cards: People are already leaving. The rites are done, the days at Mina are over, and pilgrims are heading off in every direction, home to wherever home is. Ibn Abbas remembers the moment.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stops them with a sentence: none of you should leave until the last thing you do is at the House. Not the last purchase, not the last meal. The House.
So before the road home, there's one more walk around the Ka'ba. Today, the farewell tawaf.

teach.h: LET THE LAST OF IT BE AT THE HOUSE.
teach.b: First, the rule. Ibn Abbas's report, in Sahih Muslim, is simple: let the last of your time be at the House. A pilgrim's stay ends where it began, circling the Ka'ba.

teach.h: LIGHTENED FOR A WOMAN ON HER PERIOD.
teach.b: In another report from Ibn Abbas, in Sahih al-Bukhari, people were commanded to make their last act at the House, except that it was lightened for a woman on her period. She may set out without it.
Two days ago, Safiyyah's story showed which circling couldn't be skipped. This is the one that could be lifted. Third, how the schools weigh it.
Some schools of law hold the farewell tawaf to be required of pilgrims leaving Mecca, so that missing it calls for an offering.
Others hold it to be strongly recommended. Each school reads the same reports, and each has its reasons. Fourth, the word itself.
Wada' means a farewell. Tradition calls the Prophet's own pilgrimage, the one these lessons have been following, the Farewell Pilgrimage, Hajjat al-Wada', and he did not make another.
You met that pilgrimage back on day two hundred eighty-four.
So two goodbyes fold together here: a pilgrim's goodbye to the House, and the memory of the Prophet's goodbye to his people. What the rite teaches is a way of leaving. Not slipping out the side door.
Not letting the last memory be a crowded shop or a line for the bus. Going back to the center once more, and leaving from there, with the place you're leaving as the last thing you saw.

how: Before leaving Mecca, pilgrims circle the Ka'ba one last time in the farewell tawaf; women on their period are excused from it, and the schools differ on whether it is required or strongly recommended.

o: the last circling of the Ka'ba before leaving Mecca
the Prophet's final sermon, given on the plain
a goodbye prayer said at the Prophet's grave

games.q: the farewell tawaf — tap the pairs.
p: let the last of it be at the House

s: the farewell tawaf is the same as the tawaf of Ifadah
Ifadah is the essential circling after Arafah; the farewell is the last one before leaving Mecca.
a woman on her period may leave without the farewell tawaf
Ibn Abbas reports it was lightened for her.
every school of law treats the farewell tawaf the same way
some schools hold it required; others, strongly recommended.

games.q: your rites are done and your group is packing to leave Mecca. what do you do last?
o: go back and circle the House, and leave from there.
one last trip to the market.
games.why: the Prophet said none of you should leave until the last thing you do is at the House.

practice: Think of a goodbye that's coming, the end of a job, a friend moving, a visit with a parent that ends on Sunday, or one you rushed in a parking lot or a text.
Picture how you'd want that last moment to go, who you'd look at and what you'd say. If you pray, hold that person in your du'a; if not, simply hold them in mind.

wordCard.voice: The farewell tawaf. The last circling of the Ka'ba before a pilgrim leaves Mecca, so the final act of the journey is at the House. Today's word.

orig.note: the farewell circling; wada' is a farewell.

carryVoice: Your line: goodbye to the house. The way you leave is part of the visit. Go well.
